testScopeNotes: The initial full server test found an older invariant requiring a new pot to record its own addition order. The implementation was corrected to carry food-owned history while preserving fresh order and entry conditions; all final tests pass.

The first vanilla client attempt correctly rejected a fixture action outside player reach. Moving the player next to the second station fixed the test scenario; production interaction reach is unchanged.

The final vanilla run covers the new quality, contact damage, hints-off serving, loose transfer, eating and saving workflows plus core creative/crafting/fuel checks. Other recipe regression workflows are included in the full Iris run.
The comparison screen displays real produced stacks using normal item tooltip lines; it is a test presentation, not a new production interface.
Raw ingredients, stage placement and hunger setup are test fixtures; cookedness, charring, transfer, contact damage, food effects and saving use normal game logic and real client packets.

First-meal acquisition dependencies were inspected and documented only. A complete uncheated survival route, animal-fat rendering, crop ecology and the remaining finite design scope are not marked complete.

After the full Iris run, a focused quality-only correction exempts plain rice, dough and pie from mandatory salt/soy. Final native and Iris finishing flows recook porridge and explicitly assert its real served quality; this changes no heating, fuel, cut or recipe-stage logic.
